'''James Charles Séamus Davis''' (born 22 March 1961)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Davis, J. C. Séamus|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11506008.html|url-status=dead|publisher=American Institute of Physics|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251223131844/https://history.aip.org/phn/11506008.html|archive-date=2025-12-23|access-date=2024-08-22}}</ref> is an Irish [[physicist]] whose research explores the world of [[Macroscopic quantum phenomena|macroscopic quantum physics]]. Davis concentrates upon the fundamental physics of exotic states of electronic, magnetic, atomic and space-time quantum matter. A specialty is development of innovative instrumentation to allow direct atomic-scale visualisation or perception of the macroscopic quantum phenomena that are characteristic of these states.

Davis operates two suites of ultra-low vibration laboratories, one in Beecroft Building at [[University of Oxford]] in the United Kingdom, another in the Kane Building at [[University College Cork]] in Ireland.

== Biography ==
Born in 1961 in [[Skibbereen]], [[County Cork]], Ireland, Davis was admitted to [[University College Cork]] (UCC) in 1978 to study physics under [[Frank Fahy (physicist)|Frank Fahy]], graduating with a [[Bachelor of Science]] in 1983.<ref name="NUI">{{Cite web|title=Séamus Davis|url=http://www.nui.ie/college/docs/citations/2013/nui/Seamus_Davis.pdf|url-status=dead|publisher=National University of Ireland|date=2013-12-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250905154526/http://www.nui.ie/college/docs/citations/2013/nui/Seamus_Davis.pdf|archive-date=2025-09-05}}</ref> He received a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in Physics from the [[University of California, Berkeley]], in 1989. He became a postdoctoral research associate at UC Berkeley the following year, and joined the faculty in 1993. He was appointed Professor of Physics in 2000.<ref name="CV">{{Cite web|title=Brief CV – J.C. Séamus Davis– August 2020|url=https://www.ucc.ie/en/media/academic/physics/quantummatterseamusdavis/CV-Brief-JCSeamusDavis2020.pdf|url-status=live|publisher=University College Cork|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231213015108/https://www.ucc.ie/en/media/academic/physics/quantummatterseamusdavis/CV-Brief-JCSeamusDavis2020.pdf|archive-date=2023-12-13|access-date=2026-06-20}}</ref>

From 1998 to 2002, Davis was a faculty physicist at [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]]. He then joined [[Cornell University]] as Professor of Physics in 2003, and was appointed J.G. White Distinguished Professor of Physics in 2008. In 2007, he became SUPA Distinguished Professor of Physics at the [[University of St Andrews]]. He joined [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] in 2007 as a senior physicist, and in 2009 was appointed director of [[United States Department of Energy|DOE]]'s Center for Emergent Superconductivity. In 2019, Davis became Professor of Quantum Physics at UCC, Senior Fellow of [[Wadham College, Oxford]], and Professor of Physics at the [[University of Oxford]].<ref name="CV"/>

== Research ==
Davis' overall interests focus upon macroscopic quantum physics. Active research subjects include studies of:

* Macroscopic Quantum Physics 
* AI for Quantum Matter Discovery
* Quantum & Classical Spin Liquids
* Cu/Fe High-Tc Superconductors
* Atomic-scale Electronic Fluid Flow
* Electron Pair Density Wave States
* Topological Superconductors
* Kondo Metals & Insulators

For these studies, a variety of specialised instrumentation has been developed including scanning tunneling microscopes, quantum interferometers, quantum mechanical oscillators and spin noise spectrometers. The overall strategy is to exploit distinct capabilities and facilities so as to conduct scientifically harmonized studies with complementary scientific instruments at all group locations.
